summary.en: Some short place phrases merge a preposition and an article into one word.

body.en:
From season 1, episode 1.

At the Hôtel du Tilleul, guests arrive *à la gare* and head up *au deuxième étage*, while some rooms are never rented *aux clients*. All three phrases mark a place or recipient, yet the small word at the start changes with the noun that follows.

*au* combines *à* and *le* before a masculine singular noun (*au deuxième étage*). *aux* combines *à* and *les* before any plural noun (*aux clients*). Before a feminine singular noun, *à la* stays two separate words (*à la gare*), and before a vowel or mute h you hear `à l'` (*à l'abri*).

Learn each location phrase together with its noun's gender rather than translating every English 'at' or 'to' with the same word.

On replay, compare the single vowel /o/ of *au* and *aux* with the two-syllable rhythm of *à la*.
